newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-TOM STIANSEN GETS HIS FIRST WORLD CUP SLALOM WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOM STIANSEN GETS HIS FIRST WORLD CUP SLALOM WIN.

text.p: Tom Stiansen of Norway, never better than eighth in any previous World Cup slalom, won the second one of the early season Sunday.

Stiansen, in his sixth World Cup season, held off fast-charging Thomas Sykora of Austria to win with a time of 1:45.49. Sykora, who came from behind last week to win the season's first slalom, fell just short at 1:45.65.
Thomas Stangassinger of Austria finished third in 1:45.89, ahead of Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway in 1:46.47. Michael Tritscher gave Austria three racers in the top five, clocking 1:46.81.
Aamodt took the overall World Cup lead with his fourth-place finish.

For a few fleeting seconds, it looked as if Sykora might have a come-from-behind victory. Stiansen, perhaps skiing too cautiously, lost most of his .34 first-run lead, then rallied smartly to save the race.

Stiansen's previous best in slalom was eighth place last season at Sestrieres, Italy -- his only top 10 finish in that event. Better known as a giant slalom racer, the 26-year-old twice made the podium in the longer race.
Christian Mayer of Austria, runner-up after the morning heat, abandoned the course on the second run, as did Fredrik Nyberg of Sweden, winner of Saturday's giant slalom.
